# 0. Setup

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from plotnine import *

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=12) + theme(figure_size=(7, 4)))
```

```{python}
claims  = pd.read_csv("data/claims.csv", parse_dates=["service_date"])
members = pd.read_csv("data/members.csv", parse_dates=["enroll_start", "enroll_end"])
ehr     = pd.read_csv("data/ehr_encounters.csv", parse_dates=["encounter_date"])
xwalk   = pd.read_csv("data/mrn_crosswalk.csv")
census  = pd.read_csv("data/census_zip.csv", dtype={"zip": str})
vendor  = pd.read_csv("data/vendor_sdoh.csv")

members["zip"] = members["zip"].astype(str)
members["age"] = 2026 - members["birth_year"]
```

# 1. Claims

## Net out reversals

Some claims were reversed (negative dollars). Sum each claim before doing anything else.

```{python}
claims["claim_status"].value_counts()
```

```{python}
net = (
    claims
    .groupby(["claim_id", "member_id", "service_date", "claim_type", "place_of_service", "dx1", "procedure_or_drug"], dropna=False)
    [["allowed_amt", "paid_amt"]]
    .sum()
    .reset_index()
)
net = net[net["paid_amt"] > 0]
len(claims), len(net)
```

## PMPM by plan type

```{python}
paid = net.groupby("member_id")["paid_amt"].sum()
mem = members.assign(paid=members["member_id"].map(paid).fillna(0))

pmpm = mem.groupby("plan_type")[["paid", "member_months"]].sum()
pmpm["pmpm"] = pmpm["paid"] / pmpm["member_months"]
pmpm.round(0)
```

## How concentrated is spending?

```{python}
spend = mem.sort_values("paid", ascending=False)["paid"]
top5 = spend.head(int(len(spend) * 0.05)).sum() / spend.sum()
print(f"Top 5% of members = {top5:.0%} of spend")
```

# 2. Electronic Health Records

## Link EHR to members

```{python}
ehr_m = ehr.merge(xwalk, on="mrn", how="left")
print(f"{members['member_id'].isin(ehr_m['member_id']).mean():.0%} of members have EHR data")
```

## Clean impossible BMIs

```{python}
(
    ggplot(ehr_m.dropna(subset=["bmi"]), aes("bmi"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=80) + scale_x_log10()
)
```

```{python}
ehr_m.loc[~ehr_m["bmi"].between(12, 70), "bmi"] = np.nan
```

## Who has diabetes? Three sources

```{python}
dx  = set(net.loc[net["dx1"] == "E11.9", "member_id"])                    # diagnosis (claims)
rxd = set(net.loc[net["procedure_or_drug"] == "metformin", "member_id"])  # drug (claims)
lab = set(ehr_m.loc[ehr_m["a1c"] >= 6.5, "member_id"])                    # lab (EHR)

# Among EHR-linked members: which sources flag them?
src = pd.DataFrame({"member_id": ehr_m["member_id"].unique()})
src["Dx"], src["Rx"], src["Lab"] = [src["member_id"].isin(s) for s in (dx, rxd, lab)]
src.query("Dx or Rx or Lab").value_counts(["Dx", "Rx", "Lab"])
```

# 3. Public / Census Data

```{python}
census.head()
```

```{python}
ed_n = ed.groupby("member_id").size().rename("ed_visits")
by_zip = (
    mem
    .merge(ed_n, on="member_id", how="left")
    .fillna({"ed_visits": 0})
    .groupby("zip")[["ed_visits", "member_months"]]
    .sum()
    .merge(census, on="zip")
)
by_zip["ed_per_1000"] = 12_000 * by_zip["ed_visits"] / by_zip["member_months"]

(
    ggplot(by_zip, aes("svi", "ed_per_1000"))
    + geom_smooth(method="lm") + geom_point(size=3)
    + geom_text(aes(label="county"), nudge_y=12, size=8)
    + labs(x="Social Vulnerability Index", y="ED visits per 1,000 member-years")
)
```

**Note to self:** what does the ecological fallacy warn us about here?

# 4. Vendor Data

```{python}
v = members[["member_id"]].merge(vendor, on="member_id", how="left")
print(f"Matched: {v['match_confidence'].notna().mean():.0%}  |  "
      f"High-confidence (>= 0.7): {(v['match_confidence'] >= 0.7).mean():.0%}")
```

```{python}
dat = (mem.merge(ed_n, on="member_id", how="left").fillna({"ed_visits": 0})
          .merge(census, on="zip")
          .merge(vendor, on="member_id")
          .query("match_confidence >= 0.7"))
dat["diabetes_dx"] = dat["member_id"].isin(dx).astype(int)

fit = smf.glm("ed_visits ~ food_insecurity_index + svi + age + diabetes_dx + C(plan_type)",
              data=dat, family=sm.families.Poisson(),
              offset=np.log(dat["member_months"])).fit()
np.exp(fit.params).round(3)    # incidence rate ratios (IRRs)
```
